# The relation interior of IEEE 1788, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_rel_interior_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether every member of $X$ is in the interior of $Y$, $X = [x_l, x_u]$ and $Y = [y_l, y_u]$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \subseteq \operatorname{int} Y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $y_l = y_{l0} + y_{l1}$, $y_u = y_{u0} + y_{u1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $Y = [y_l, y_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $y_l = +\infty$ and $y_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $y_l \le y_u$, $y_l < +\infty$, $y_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when every member of $X$ is in the interior of $Y$: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_rel_interior_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_rel_interior_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_rel_interior_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the stored bounds compared, and a test of emptiness (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_rel_interior_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_rel_interior_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md).

```
# The relation interior of IEEE 1788 of two intervals with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md,
# "Comparisons", the relations of IEEE 1788, and "IEEE 1788"): every member of X is in the interior
# of Y. The empty set is interior to every interval; otherwise y_l < x_l, or both are -inf, and x_u
# < y_u, or both are +inf (an infinite bound is inside an equal infinite bound, the rule of Table
# 4.5). With the empty set as Y, no nonempty X is interior: y_l = +inf is below no bound. Exact. For
# every precision.

ex = eq(xl0, const inf)
mi = neg(const inf)
la = lt_2_2(yl0, yl1, xl0, xl1)
lb = eq(yl0, mi)
lc = eq(xl0, mi)
ld = and(lb, lc)
lo = or(la, ld)
ua = lt_2_2(xu0, xu1, yu0, yu1)
ub = eq(xu0, const inf)
uc = eq(yu0, const inf)
ud = and(ub, uc)
hi = or(ua, ud)
lu = and(lo, hi)
m  = or(ex, lu)
```
